content: The provided text is a detailed description of drug interactions, focusing on how specific medications, particularly omeprazole and clarithromycin, affect the metabolism, efficacy, and safety of other drugs. 1. Omeprazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is significant, and alternative medications should be considered. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, the axitinib dose should be reduced by 50%, and the patient should be closely monitored. 2. Clarithromycin also increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50% and monitor the patient closely. 3. Both azithromycin and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use these drugs with caution and monitor the patient closely for cardiac effects. 4. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It may also decrease their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but alternative drugs should be considered. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 8. Clarithromycin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and the patient’s ECG should be closely monitored. Clarithromycin also increases the levels of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 9. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Adjust the therapy by increasing the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when coadministered with proton pump inhibitors. Monitor the patient closely. 10. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and coadministration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the risk or severity of adverse effects. Monitor the patient closely. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate according to its prescribing information. 12. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor the patient closely. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Monitor the patient closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 15. Clarithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor the patient closely. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 17. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 18. Omeprazole increases the levels of bismuth subsalicylate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Clarithromycin increases the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Blessed thistle decreases the effects of omeprazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Bortezomib also increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin and omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 23. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of bosutinib through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor the patient for adverse reactions. 25. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Omeprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Adjust therapy and monitor the patient closely. Extended-release budesonide tablet dissolution is pH-dependent. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. It also decreases clarithromycin levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels of cabergoline by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If required, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the calcifediol dose and monitor serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Cannabidiol increases the levels of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor the patient closely. 39. Clarithromycin increases the levels of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 40. Omeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 43. Carbamazepine decreases the levels of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 44. Omeprazole decreases the levels of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the cariprazine dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefotaxime, and cefpodoxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Use caution and monitor the patient closely.
